mysql_backend.instructions: Select the MySQL descriptor grammar for offline compilation.

criteria.live_server_prepare: Prepare every descriptor on a live server while building, accepting the server dependency.
criteria.tidb_parser: Pin TiDB's standalone parser module, whose nodes and markers carry origin offsets and modes.
criteria.vitess_parser: Pin Vitess's serving parser from its monorepo, confirming span access experimentally.

sqlite_backend.instructions: Select the SQLite descriptor grammar for offline compilation.

criteria.engine_api_prepare: Trust engine prepare behavior, authorizer signals, and handle metadata without spans.
criteria.antlr_grammar: Generate Go from the maintained ANTLR SQLite grammar and regenerate under a JVM.
criteria.treesitter_mirror: Follow the young parse.y mirror with committed C, blessing license, and JVM-free regeneration.

state: The G-SQL gate must pick compile-time grammar backends for SQLite and MySQL descriptors in the Can compiler, which is written in Go and builds offline. PostgreSQL sets the precedent: pg_query_go/v6 v6.2.2 embeds generated C behind cgo at major 17, version 170007, and yields statement spans, byte-offset tokens, node kind, LIMIT shape, RETURNING flags, and verbatim failures that callers classify structurally per compiler/internal/sql/parser.go. Any new backend has to match that interface: statements, spans, kind, limit shape, returning, failures. The shared contract admits one statement only, SELECT for one/optional/many and a mutation for execute, contiguous parameters ending in a single top-level LIMIT site, zero RETURNING clauses, full-byte tiling segments, and a pinned version stamp. Evidence lives in a 37-statement corpus at docs/bun-integration/asap/evidence/sql-corpus.json: 12 postgresql plus 13 sqlite plus 12 mysql entries mixing acceptance and rejection, exercising quoted semicolons, comment forms, dollar-like decoys, backticks, backslash escapes, every SQLite placeholder spelling, CTEs, RETURNING, stacked statements, and LIMIT shapes. Span precision dominates the safety case. Skipping a genuine site trips arity and stops the build, which is safe, whereas inventing a site rebinds every later value silently, which no later engine prepare can catch since preparation only demotes extra acceptance to query_failed. Rejecting a good statement just asks the author to rephrase. On the MySQL side, vitess_parser offers the query-serving grammar of Vitess at v0.24.3 from 2026-09-03 under Apache-2.0, but it sits in an enormous module and nobody has verified offset access for placeholders, so spans need a spike. tidb_parser offers TiDB's production grammar as the standalone module github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/parser at v0.0.0-20260923074046 from 2026-09-23 under Apache-2.0 with few dependencies; its Parse(sql, charset, collation) hands back statement nodes, all nodes answer OriginTextPosition, markers arrive with offsets, and SQL mode lives in the lexer. live_server_prepare would compile against a reachable server, forfeiting offline hermetic builds, aiming arbitrary build-time SQL at user data against gate step 4, and leaning on message text. On the SQLite side, engine_api_prepare leans on a genuine embedded engine: the authorizer trick establishes validity, prepare tails split statements, and readonly plus counts plus names come free. Yet spans, LIMIT position, and RETURNING stay out of reach, PRAGMA writes masquerade as mutations, EXPLAIN masquerades as SELECT, and the shared SQLITE_ERROR code forces message sniffing to tell syntax from resolution apart. antlr_grammar pairs the community grammars-v4 sql/sqlite grammar, touched in March and June 2026 for precedence and ALTER TABLE, with runtime antlr4-go v4.13.1; generated Go would be committed and pinned, but every regeneration demands a JVM that does not exist here since /usr/bin/java is a dead stub, and the grammar is a reimplementation needing engine-differential proof. treesitter_mirror is defin/tree-sitter-sqlite3, a production-by-production mirror of parse.y and tokenize.c tracking 3.47.0, dedicated under a blessing license, shipping 5.8MB of parser.c plus grammar.json, scanner.c, and corpus tests; it rides the same committed-C plus cgo rails as pg_query_go in a build that already enables cgo, and its CLI regenerates without Java, but the project is four months old with one author (2026-05-03 to 2026-07-26), so the differential still applies. Research surfaced no maintained pure-Go SQLite grammar. Splitters, cross-dialect libpg_query reuse, translate-then-validate, bespoke subset grammars, and Bun subprocess validation at build time are excluded. Whoever wins must clear the corpus, then survive a bun:sqlite fixture-schema prepare differential on syntax for SQLite immediately and a live-service differential for MySQL in B1-03.
